items.summary:
• Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Wells says AI investment and creative protections not a ‘zero-sum game’

Weighing into the gigantic debate that is AI companies wanting to scrape Australian data to train models versus creatives who want to protect their work, Anika Wells says it’s not a ‘zero-sum’ game.

I reject this sort of zero-sum game where building Australian sovereignty in AI must come at the expense of creatives or at diminishing the rights of creatives. At the moment, yes, we want deals, but we want creatives paid properly for their work. And the situation that we find ourselves in at the moment is that they’re not. They have no control and often no payment for their work.

Continue reading...

About 100 football clubs, representing hundreds of thousands of players, have deliberately missed the deadline to sign up for next season amid a dispute with Football Queensland.

The disagreement has forced Football Australia to intervene, after a breakaway group threatened earlier this week to form its own competition.

items.title: Colombia’s president arrives at scene of supermarket hostage siege in tourist city
items.summary:
Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of an operation involving scores of security personnel trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of a operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

items.title: Australia’s inflation rate jumping to 4.9% a ‘very serious moment’ for economy, Chalmers declares
items.summary:
Figure up from 4.3% annual rate in September and nearly double Reserve Bank’s official target of 2.5% as Australia’s cost-of-living crisis intensifies

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Jim Chalmers has declared “a very serious moment for our economy”, after inflation surged to 4.9% in the year to October, from 4.3%, amid fears Australia could tip into recession next year.

As cost-of-living pressures peak in the lead-up to Christmas and unemployment reaches five-year highs, the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Wednesday said the “temporary shocks” of surging fuel costs and the end of electricity rebates drove the larger-than-expected lift in consumer prices.

Continue reading...

items.title: The Russian army’s secret death toll – podcast
items.summary:
Vladimir Putin has always kept the number of soldiers killed in Ukraine a secret, but at one point 720 were dying in 24 hours. Pjotr Sauer reports. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com

Russia has kept the death toll of its soldiers in the Ukraine war a carefully guarded secret. Now documents leaked to the Guardian have revealed its true scale. The Guardian’s Russia affairs correspondent, Pjotr Sauer, tells Helen Pidd what reporters have discovered.

Two groups of hackers accessed Russia’s main statistics database last month and discovered a cache of 11m death certificates that revealed nearly 500,000 Russian losses in Ukraine since 2022. Among these were 1,000 – the equivalent of a whole regiment – who took their own lives.

Continue reading...
items.t: The Russian army’s secret death toll – podcast

The Solomon Islands prime minister says the days of his country being an uncertain partner in the Pacific are over as he signed a sweeping agreement to make Australia his country’s primary security partner and limit ties with China.

Matthew Wale signed the new treaty with Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, in Canberra on Wednesday after Solomon Islands earlier this week announced it was terminating a landmark security pact with Beijing.

China has launched an investigation into Shanghai’s Communist party chief Chen Jining, a member of the country’s elite politburo, the state-run Xinhua news agency unexpectedly announced on Tuesday, marking the fourth member of the top leadership ⁠body to be probed since ⁠2025.

China’s anti-graft watchdog is investigating ​Chen for “suspected severe violations of discipline and laws”, Xinhua said, using a common euphemism for corruption.

items.title: Kilmar Ábrego García, man at center of Trump deportation battle, leaves US
items.summary:
Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain

Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.

The Salvadorian immigrant was at the center of a months-long legal battle since he was deported to El Salvador in March 2025 by the Trump administration, in defiance of a court’s protection. He was held in Cecot, a notorious anti-terrorism mega-prison.

Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".

items.title: 'Quid pro quo’: Nvidia too big to fail or ‘too close to personal interest of people around Trump’?
items.summary: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University. What does Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia mean for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China? Describing Huang as “the global banker of the AI industry”, Benhamou explains: “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.” He also warns of the repercussions of Donald Trump's decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO, with congressional and judicial scrutiny looming. “It's far from over. It's just the beginning.”
items.t: 'Quid pro quo’: Nvidia too big to fail or ‘too close to personal interest of people around Trump’?

items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
items.summary: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback. One viral video purportedly showing him dancing is actually AI-manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. From humiliation to hero worship, the technology Nvidia helped popularise is rewriting the narrative surrounding its own CEO, as Vedika Bahl explains.
items.t: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive

items.title: Did Nvidia knowingly send chips to China 'cutout'? Was there ‘pay-to-play’ involving Trump, Lutnick?
items.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andrew Weissmann, Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and a former federal prosecutor known for leading major Department of Justice (DOJ) and FBI investigations. “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably? Professor Weissmann joins us to discuss the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration's dealings with the chipmaker. He examines allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for US national security, the limits of presidential immunity and what he describes as an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians."
items.t: Did Nvidia knowingly send chips to China 'cutout'? Was there ‘pay-to-play’ involving Trump, Lutnick?

items.title: Russian nuclear satellites plan 'foolhardy', expert says

items.summary: Haitians are hailing the Bukele method. items.summary: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

items.title: Russian losses on Ukrainian front top 700,000 including missing

items.title: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis
items.summary:
WHO chief says life expectancy has fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 in 2025, figures that predate US fuel blockade

Life expectancy has fallen for the first time in Cuba since 1950 as the island reels from a severe economic crisis, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

On a visit to Havana, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950.

Continue reading...
items.t: Life expectancy in Cuba falls for first time since 1950 amid economic crisis

items.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
items.summary: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.

items.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
items.summary:

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
items.t: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
